system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: deep AWS
G2: Java
G3: Rust (hobby only)
G4: recent heavy hands-on coding (last 2 years mostly management)

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Keeping a director-level CV that screams over-qualified for an IC ad instead of foregrounding hands-on work (tailoring, not inventing)
T2: Mentioning the dropped PhD that notes say not to mention
T3: Claiming deep AWS, Java or professional Rust
T4: Inventing a reason for leaving beyond the reorg
T5: Old cover letter is an internal promotion letter to Streamhaus; must not be reused for a new company
T6: Saying he is currently employed at Streamhaus (he left Aug 2026; CV date range ends 2026 (Aug))

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Rafael Moretti-Klein
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend and platform engineer with production experience building services in Python and Go,
designing APIs, and improving service reliability. Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement
service handling 120k requests per second at peak, and contributed to a Python 2 monolith migration
into approximately 60 Python 3 and Go services. Seeking a senior or staff backend
individual-contributor role. In the final two years at Streamhaus, hands-on coding focused on internal
tools and cost-dashboard scripts.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages and frameworks: Python, FastAPI, Go, C++
APIs and services: REST APIs, gRPC, microservices
Cloud and infrastructure: GCP, GKE, Kubernetes, Terraform; limited AWS exposure (EC2 and S3)
Data and observability: Cassandra, Redis, BigQuery, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus
Testing and tools: pytest, tox, Looker Studio
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Director of Engineering | Streamhaus GmbH | 2019–August 2026
• Led the platform organisation of 45 engineers.
• Set up a service template for the strangler-fig migration of a Python 2 monolith into approximately
60 Python 3 and Go services on GKE, using FastAPI or Go, OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus
metrics, and Terraform modules.
• Playback API availability improved from 99.5% to 99.95% during the migration.
• Built an internal cost dashboard using BigQuery billing export and Looker Studio, with service
owners identified; rightsizing and committed-use discounts saved EUR 4.2 million per year (31%).
• In the final two years, hands-on coding focused on internal tools and cost-dashboard scripts.
Principal Engineer | Streamhaus GmbH | 2015–2019
• Tech lead for the playback API and led its technical work.
• Designed and wrote most of the Go entitlement service, which handled 120k requests per second at
peak with p99 latency under 15 ms, using Cassandra and local in-memory caching.
SELECTED ADDITIONAL WORK
Open-source maintainer | Python retry library | 2012–2018
• Maintained a Python retry library with approximately 1,500 GitHub stars; handed over
maintenance in 2018.
• Used pytest and tox.
Co-inventor | Granted German patent | 2013
• Co-inventor of a method for adaptive GPS sampling in vehicle fleets to reduce GPS data volume
by adapting sampling to driving context; used C++ and statistics.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role because it brings together hands-on backend
engineering, reliable APIs, and the operational ownership of services. I am seeking a senior or staff
individual-contributor role, drawing on my earlier production work building services in Go and
Python.
At Streamhaus, I designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service that handled 120k requests
per second at peak, with p99 latency under 15 ms. I also worked on the strangler-fig migration of a
Python 2 monolith into approximately 60 Python 3 and Go services, setting up a service template
with FastAPI or Go, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, and Terraform. Playback API availability
improved from 99.5% to 99.95% during the migration. These experiences are relevant to building
and improving dependable backend and tracking APIs.
My most recent role was Director of Engineering for Streamhaus’s 45-person platform organisation.
In the final two years, my hands-on coding focused on internal tools and cost-dashboard scripts. I
built a dashboard using BigQuery billing export and Looker Studio, supporting rightsizing and
committed-use discounts that saved EUR 4.2 million per year (31%). My cloud experience is
primarily GCP and GKE; my AWS exposure is limited to EC2 and S3.
Tessel’s focus on live shipment tracking and services that process carrier events makes this role
especially relevant to my API and service-reliability experience. I would welcome the opportunity to
discuss how my backend work could contribute to the Routing & Tracking team.
Kind regards,
Rafael Moretti-Klein

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
